subject: Re: AcmeHealth - pricing & context-length profiling follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: AcmeHealth discovery follow-up - context length + token volumes

Hi Alicia,

Thanks again for taking the time today - great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned:

What I heard from the call:
- Primary use case: clinical note summarization + live assistant for care coordinators.
- Typical interaction: user pastes a patient thread (varied lengths) then asks for a concise summary + suggested follow-ups.
- Volume signals: pilot ~500k tokens/month, projected to scale to 10-12M tokens/month in 6-12 months.
- Compliance: PHI remains in scope; you need SOC2 evidence and option for private deployment later.

For pricing & sizing we need a quick profile from your side so we can scope unit economics and recommend 8k/32k/128k needs:
1) Avg prompt tokens (typical user request, before model completes)
2) Avg completion tokens (expected model output length)
3) Monthly token volume today (approx) and target in 6-12 months
4) Percent of requests that need extended context (32k / 128k) vs standard (8k)
5) Any QoS/SLA expectations or peak concurrency windows

If you can reply with the data above (rough numbers are fine) I'll draft a pricing sketch (target $/1M tokens) and a short eval plan (sample traces, quick perf run on 8k/32k). Attaching a 1-page context-length survey - if you can share back a filled copy or paste answers here that'll be perfect.

Next steps we suggested on the call:
- You (AcmeHealth) share sample traces or fill the survey by Tue 29 Jun
- We (Redwood) run a quick perf + cost estimate, and send a pricing preview
- Rishi (SE) to join an evaluation call with engineering if performance looks good

Thanks - talk soon.


Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@acmehealth.com>

Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth - pricing & context-length profiling follow-up

Hi Marissa,

Great recap - below are the numbers we can share immediately (high level/approx):

1) Avg prompt tokens: ~320 tokens (this includes the pasted patient thread + user question).
2) Avg completion tokens: ~450 tokens (summary + suggested follow-ups, tends to be concise).
3) Monthly token volume: today ~500k tokens/month; target 10-12M tokens/month within 9 months (depends on pilot outcome).
4) Extended context needs: ~92% of requests fit within 8k.
   - ~7% will hit 32k (long care-coordinator threads with embedded attachments we convert to text).
   - ~1% are very long legal/consent bundles where 128k would be helpful (we estimate ~500-1k requests/month once scaled).
5) SLA/peaks: typical working hours 08:00-19:00 PT; peak concurrency ~20-30 concurrent requests during roster syncs. We need <300ms additional tail latency if possible and predictable burst handling.

Budget range: leadership gave a preliminary ballpark of $6k-12k/month for the pilot phase (this is flexible based on unit economics). For long-term target, we're hoping for unit costs in the ballpark of $700-1,200 per 1M tokens (open to negotiated committed tiers).

We can upload a sample of anonymized traces (stripped PHI) - working that with engineering now. Expect a Drive link by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Alicia

Alicia Torres
Director, Product Operations | AcmeHealth
alicia.torres@acmehealth.com

Subject: Re: AcmeHealth - pricing & context-length profiling follow-up

Alicia - this is super helpful, thanks for the concrete numbers. High-level read and proposed next steps below.

Quick read on numbers:
- Volume/target: 10-12M tokens/month aligns with a mid-sized pilot converting to production.
- Token mix: heavy 8k use (92%) with a small but meaningful 32k tail (~7%) and a tiny 128k footprint (~1%).

Pricing sketch (preliminary, subject to eval):
- Target unit economics we can aim for: $800 / 1M tokens for standard 8k profile at committed volume tiers (10M+/mo).
- 32k context requests: price uplift vs 8k (we'd propose ~1.4x the 8k rate for 32k by default).
- 128k requests: higher uplift depending on memory & inference path (proposal ~2.0x-2.5x the 8k base).

This maps to an approximate range: if you hit 10M tokens/mo with the mix you stated, estimated spend ~ $8k/mo (ballpark) - which fits within your leadership pilot range. We'll produce a modeled sheet showing exact math.

Next steps:
1) We'll intake the anonymized traces you mentioned (Drive link) and run a 1-2 day perf + cost run across 8k/32k/128k configurations.
2) Rishi will propose a quick evaluation plan and recommend quantized variants or model family that fit your latency/quality tradeoffs.
3) We'll send a pricing preview XLS and a short eval timeline (two business days after we get traces).

Attaching the preview sheet and an outline for the eval. If that looks good we can schedule the technical sync (Rishi + your engineering team) for Wed or Thu.


Marissa

Hi Alicia / Marissa - quick technical note based on Alicia's numbers and Marissa's pricing sketch.

Thanks for the breakdown Alicia - that helps a lot. A few practical recommendations:
- Given avg prompt ~320 / completion ~450, standard 8k sequences will cover the vast majority with good batching efficiency.
- The 7% 32k tail suggests we should evaluate a mixed routing approach: keep 8k-optimized endpoints for most traffic, route 32k requests to a separate pool (quantized / different batching), and reserve 128k for a narrow, provisioned path.
- For cost estimates, quantized FP16/INT8 model variants will materially reduce $/token for the 8k path and are worth benchmarking during the eval.

Operational ask from our side: please include 24-48 hours of request traces (sampled) showing prompt/completion token counts and a handful of the long documents that require 32k/128k. That will let us model token distribution and produce a tight $/1M estimate.

I can join the technical sync Wednesday 10:00-11:00 PT (or Thursday 14:00-15:00 PT) - does either work?

Thanks - Rishi
